rules.title: Writ datatype definition
rules.statement: A datatype item is `[pub[(vis)]] eidos NAME [<type-params>] { field_def_or_doc* }`. It declares a Writ-fabric datatype with named/repeat-group fields; the optional generic parameter list and visibility marker are accepted.
examples: pub eidos Point<T> { x: T, y: T }

rules.title: Explicit datatype instantiation declaration
rules.statement: `[pub[(vis)]] eidos TYPE_REF ;` (no body) is an explicit-instantiation declaration that binds metadata annotations (e.g. `#[type_code=N]`) to a concrete generic instantiation, e.g. `#[type_code=42] datatype Array<i32>;`.

rules.title: Explicit genos/trait specialization declaration
rules.statement: `[pub[(vis)]] <trait-kw> TYPE_REF ;` (no body) binds annotations to a logical-family (genos) specialization of a concrete trait instantiation; implementing eidos inherit the metadata via impl.

rules.title: Unit struct declaration
rules.statement: `[pub] struct IDENT ;` declares a zero-field (unit) struct. A bare IDENT immediately followed by `;` is a unit struct; `struct Foo<...>;` (IDENT then `<`) is instead parsed as an explicit instantiation. This rule MUST be matched before struct_inst.

rules.title: Explicit struct instantiation declaration
rules.statement: `[pub[(vis)]] struct TYPE_REF ;` where TYPE_REF carries type arguments (e.g. `struct Foo<i64>;`) is an explicit-instantiation declaration binding annotations to a generic struct instantiation. The dedicated `instantiate Foo<T>;` form is preferred.
rules.divergence: A6: see B-item-92 — bare `struct Foo;` is the unit struct, generic form kept for the unbound-typevar diagnostic

rules.title: Named-field struct definition
rules.statement: `[pub[(vis)]] struct IDENT [<type-params>] [where-clause] { field_def_or_doc* method_def_or_doc* }` defines a struct with named fields, optional generics, an optional where-clause, and optional inline method definitions.
examples: pub struct S<T> where T: Clone { x: T, fn get(&self) -> &T { &self.x } }

rules.title: Tuple struct definition
rules.statement: `[pub[(vis)]] struct IDENT [<type-params>] ( tuple_field (, tuple_field)* ) ;` defines a tuple struct whose fields are types only; field names are synthesized as "0","1",… so `foo.0` and pattern `Foo(a,b)` work uniformly with named-field structs. Each tuple_field may carry its own `pub`.

rules.title: Where-clause only on IDENT-name struct alternatives
rules.statement: A struct/enum definition where-clause is accepted only on the IDENT-NAME alternatives, not on the antiquot (NAME_VAR / `#`-prefixed) alternatives, because WHERE and NAME_VAR share an AST slot.
rules.uncertainty: Slot-sharing is an implementation constraint surfaced as a grammar restriction.

rules.title: Union definition
rules.statement: `[pub[(vis)]] union IDENT [<type-params>] [where-clause] { field_def_or_doc* }` defines a union with named fields and optional generics. It is collected internally as a struct flagged `is_union`; no tuple shape, no methods.
examples: union U { a: i32, b: f32 }

rules.title: Named field definition
rules.statement: A struct field is `[pub] IDENT : TYPE_REF [,]`. The contextual keywords `new` and `null` are also accepted as field names. A trailing comma is permitted.

rules.title: Variadic field
rules.statement: A field of form `IDENT ... : TYPE_REF` marks a variadic field (IS_VARIADIC).

rules.title: Repeat-group field (quote)
rules.statement: `#( field_def ),*` and `#( field_def )*` denote a repeat-group of field definitions (REPEAT_GROUP, OP=1 comma-separated / OP=0 plain), for use in quoted item bodies.

rules.title: Extern block
rules.statement: `[unsafe] extern ["ABI"] { extern_block_item* }` groups same-ABI externs. The optional ABI string applies to all items in the block (inherited at splice). The Rust-2024 `unsafe extern` marker is accepted with no extra semantics.
examples: unsafe extern "C" { fn puts(s: *const u8) -> i32; }

rules.title: Extern block item (fn / static)
rules.statement: Inside an extern block, items use bare `fn IDENT(params [, ...]) [-> T] ;` (no `extern` keyword; trailing `, ...` makes it variadic) or `static [mut] IDENT : T ;`. The produced extern fn carries no ABI of its own; an extern static with no value is marked external (no initializer).

rules.title: Standalone extern fn declaration
rules.statement: `extern ["ABI"] fn IDENT(params [, ...]) [-> T] ;` declares a single FFI function carrying its ABI string verbatim. A trailing `, ...` makes it variadic. Omitting the ABI string selects the default (Logos-internal) calling convention.

rules.title: Where clause
rules.statement: `where where_pred (, where_pred)*`. A predicate is `<subject> : trait_bound (+ trait_bound)*` where subject is an associated-type ref, a reference type (`&T`, incl. `for<'a> &'a T`), or a plain type-param; or it is a bare type_param.

rules.title: Visibility marker pub / pub(module)
rules.statement: Item visibility is `pub` (fully exported) or `pub(IDENT)` where IDENT is a contextual keyword validated == "module" in sema, meaning module-linkage: visible to other packages of the SAME module but not exported to consumers.
rules.divergence: Logos uses `pub(module)` for module-linkage; Rust uses `pub(crate)`/path-restricted visibilities.

rules.title: Function definition
rules.statement: A function item is `[pub[(vis)]] [unsafe] fn NAME [<type-params>] ( [param_list] ) [-> T] [where-clause] block`. NAME may be IDENT or the contextual keywords `new`/`null`. The where-clause and return type are optional.
examples: pub unsafe fn f<T>(x: T) -> T where T: Copy { x }

rules.title: Function with antiquoted name
rules.statement: `[pub] [unsafe] fn #(expr) [<type-params>] ( [params] ) [-> T] block` carries an expr-TOM name (NAME_VAR), valid only inside a quote body; these alts omit the where-clause because NAME_VAR and WHERE share a slot.

rules.title: Parameter list trailing comma
rules.statement: A parameter list is `param (, param)* (,)?`, but a trailing comma is forbidden when immediately followed by `...` (the variadic marker), so `, ...` separators are unambiguous.

rules.title: Self-receiver / ref-binding parameter shorthand
rules.statement: A parameter may be `&[mut] IDENT` (reference binding, type elided), `ref IDENT : T`, or `mut IDENT : T` (mutable local binding, mutability invisible to callers).

rules.title: Pattern-binding parameters
rules.statement: A parameter may bind an irrefutable pattern: a tuple-destructure `(a, b, ...) : T`, a struct pattern `Name { f, .. } : T`, or a slice pattern `[h, t] : T`. Refutable patterns at the fn boundary are rejected in sema with the same diagnostic as for `let`.

rules.title: Variadic parameter
rules.statement: `IDENT : T ...` marks a variadic parameter (IS_VARIADIC); plain `IDENT : T` is the ordinary typed parameter.

rules.title: Type-reference ordered choice
rules.statement: A type reference resolves by ordered choice: antiquot, typeof, cfg-slot-assoc, cfg-slot, writ-array, writ-map, pointer, array, slice, tagged, dyn, reference, impl-Trait, unit, never, closure, fn-pointer, tuple, paren, qualified-assoc, assoc-type-ref, then simple type. Associated-type forms precede simple_type so `T::Item` matches before `T`.

rules.title: Parenthesized type
rules.statement: `( T )` is a parenthesized type, distinct from `()` (unit), `(T,)` (1-tuple) and `(T1,T2)` (n-tuple); sema unwraps it to its inner type T.

rules.title: impl Trait type
rules.statement: `impl Trait`, `impl Trait<args>`, and `impl Fn(args) [-> R]` are accepted in type position; an impl-Trait parameter desugars to a synthetic generic parameter bounded by the same trait (Fn-family args→PARAMS, return→RET_TYPE, generic args→TYPE_PARAMS).

rules.title: Type-level cfg-slot projection
rules.statement: `<type:CFG.path>` projects, at mono-time, the type stored at a path within a WritStatic-typed type-level binding. Path steps are `.IDENT` (string key), `.INTEGER` (int key) and `.[INTEGER]` (array index). At least one path step is required. `<type:CFG.SLOT>::Assoc` projects an associated type on the slot base.

rules.title: Writ literal / typed array / typed map types
rules.statement: `@{...}` at type position is a WritStatic value literal type (LIT_WSTATIC). `<Elem>[]` is a Writ typed-array type and `<K[,V]>{}` is a Writ typed-map type (used in `as` casts).

rules.title: Type antiquotation
rules.statement: `$ident` in type position is a type antiquotation valid only inside `quote_ty! { ... }`; resolving it elsewhere is an error.

rules.title: typeof type
rules.statement: `typeof(expr)` is the compile-time type of expr; the expression is not evaluated.

rules.title: Associated-type projection
rules.statement: `T::Item` and `T::Item<A,B>` (GAT with type args) are associated-type references; the `::Name[<args>]` tail may chain one or more times. `<T as Trait>::Assoc` is the fully-qualified form, with the disambiguating trait recorded for resolution.

rules.title: tagged thin pointer type
rules.statement: `&tagged<T> Name` is a thin tag-dispatched pointer: a type_code tag is stored in memory before the object, and call sites read the tag, look up the dispatch table, and call indirectly.

rules.title: dyn trait-object type
rules.statement: `dyn Trait`, `&dyn Trait`, `&mut dyn Trait` (optionally lifetime-annotated and HRTB-quantified `for<'a>`) form trait objects (fat pointer: data + vtable). Type args use `<...>`; Fn-family `dyn Fn(args)[-> R]` puts args in PARAMS/return in RET_TYPE. Trailing `+ Ident` (auto-trait, e.g. Send/Sync) and `+ 'lt` (lifetime) bounds are accepted; auto-trait bounds are enforced at unsize coercion, lifetime bounds are recorded but not enforced.

rules.title: Slice type
rules.statement: `&[T]` and `&mut [T]` are slice types (fat pointer: ptr + len); an explicit lifetime `&'a [T]` / `&'a mut [T]` is accepted (captured but not distinctly enforced).

rules.title: Reference types
rules.statement: `&T`, `&mut T`, `&'a T`, `&'a mut T` are safe borrow-checked reference types. `&&T` / `&&mut T` (no whitespace, tokenized as AND) denote double-references; arbitrary-depth `& & … T` stacks are accepted at type position.

rules.title: Closure type
rules.statement: `|T1, T2| -> R` is a closure type used in parameter annotations; the zero-arg form `|| -> R` is accepted (the `||` token is split).
rules.divergence: A6: Rust spells closures via Fn-family bounds; Logos has a dedicated `|..|->R` closure type syntax.

rules.title: Function-pointer type
rules.statement: `fn(T1,T2) -> R` is a bare function-pointer type. Qualifiers/prefixes are accepted: `unsafe fn(...)` (IS_UNSAFE), `extern "ABI" fn(...)` (ABI threaded to the calling convention), and `for<'a> fn(...)` (HRTB binders captured for future region inference).
